data.why: The dashboard reads its own bundled parquet time series and static_data (geojson, shapefiles, pre-rendered scene PNGs) from the repo, so no uploads are needed; the only missing piece was an empty .streamlit/secrets.toml so st.secrets.get() can fall back to keyless basemap tiles instead of raising StreamlitSecretNotFoundError.

goals: Read the headline KPI cards for each catchment on the Overview page
Compare the Enguri and Zhinvali catchments on the overview map (AOI boundary, glaciers, rivers, reservoir)
Follow reservoir water area and snow/glacier area over time on the Time Series page, noting cloud gaps and NaN guard dates
Step through DSWx-S1 (radar water) and DSWx-HLS (optical snow/ice) scenes on the Scene Browser's date slider
Judge data quality per date via valid-pixel coverage, cloud cover and the reservoir NaN guard
Compare how the snow and glacier signal (HLS) differs in cadence and gaps from the water signal (S1)

review.summary: The tree is a faithful, well-evidenced map of the dashboard: its phases match the README's three pages plus a sensible quality-check stage, and all ten screens I opened show what their nodes claim. It needs two small fixes before filing: correct the t14 wording that confuses the S1 coverage gate with the reservoir guard, and add a task that relates the snow series to the reservoir series, since the goal claims the tool is for that.
